title: I tested 15 years of daily S&P net GEX. Low gamma predicts the size of tomorrows move, not the direction.
author: person-person12
selftext:
Negative gamma gets posted as a sell signal every time net GEX goes red. Dealers are short gamma, they chase price, so the index drops. I wanted to know whether the direction half of that has ever been true.

I took every daily S&P 500 net GEX reading in [Agenticks](https://www.agenticks.ca/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=autopilot&utm_content=ai_trading), **3,912 trading days from 2 May 2011 to 19 Nov 2026**, sorted those days into deciles by the reading, and measured the next days move on the index.

**Size of the next move, by decile** (1 is the lowest gamma, under +$0.1B, 10 is above +$6.8B):

* decile 1: average absolute move **1.49%**
* decile 5: 0.56%
* decile 10: 0.51%

The bottom tenth travels about **three times as far** as the top tenth. That half of the folklore holds up and it isnt subtle.

**Direction, exact same days:**

* decile 1: average next day return **+0.115%**, red 46.5% of the time
* decile 10: average **-0.019%**, red 49.0% of the time

The 347 days where net GEX was outright negative averaged **+0.115%** the day after, with 46.7% of them closing red. Positive gamma days averaged +0.042% and closed red 45.7% of the time. Low gamma came out very slightly green on average across fifteen years.

Its like being told the road is icy. You now know how far the car slides if anything goes wrong, you still dont know which way its pointed.

Where the bearish read earns something is the tail, and only the tail. 129 days in the sample were followed by a drop worse than 2%, and **42 of them sat in the bottom decile**. A tenth of the days carried a third of the 2% down days. The worst single day after a decile 1 reading was **-11.98%**, against -5.89% for decile 10.

One thing worth flagging about the measurement itself. This is the published daily index level series, so it is the whole S&P book once a day, not intraday dealer positioning at a strike. A flip at 2pm on a 0DTE chain is a different number and this test says nothing about it.
